replacements.value: Biblical violence, eternal punishment, and forgiveness create unresolved proportional-justice tensions: finite wrongdoing can receive infinite punishment while victims may be excluded, weakening Christianity’s claim to a coherent divine moral character.

Dillahunty could compare how probable each cited fact would be if Christianity were true with its probability under historical and psychological alternatives. Evidence shared equally by rival explanations has a likelihood ratio near one and therefore contributes little discriminatory weight, even when many observations are accumulated. Distinctive evidence would need to be substantially more expected under Christianity and sufficiently independent to avoid double-counting. This reframing replaces the categorical claim that there is no evidence with the more defensible conclusion that the offered evidence provides little comparative support, directly meeting the cumulative case on probabilistic terms.
